newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends up strongly on heat, natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends up strongly on heat, natgas.

text.p: NYMEX June electricity futures finished strongly higher Wednesday, reaching new contract highs based on climbing physical power prices and a rise in natural gas futures values, industry sources said.
NYMEX electricity futures front months have been moving higher since mid-April, and players said they expect the climb to continue, at least over the short term.
"Power trends, so don't get in its way," said one electricity futures trader.

June Palo Verde (PV) ended up $1.05 at $24.15 per megawatt hour (MWh) after reaching a new contract high of $24.30 and a low of $23.75, while July PV closed up 70 cents at $26.30 after hitting a new high of $26.60 and a low of $26.10 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds ended the day up between 10 and 71 cents.

June California Oregon Border (COB) closed up $1.08 at $18.10 after hitting a new contract high of $18.15 and a low of $17.65, while July COB was up 80 cents at $19.15 after hitting a new high of $19.30 and a low $18.90 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds finished up 10 to 78 cents.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 228 COB and 701 PV contracts traded.
Cash power prices, particularily in the Southwest, continued to strengthen on high air-conditioning demand due to hot weather in the interior section of the region.
Firm, peak power prices at COB for Thursday firmed to $18.50-21.00 a MWh from yesterday's $17.75-18.75, while those at PV rocketed to $33.00-36.00 per MWh from yesterday's $26.50-28.50.
"The heat is creating some loads," said one futures trader.
Natural gas prices also gave some support to electricity, with NYMEX June Henry Hub futures ending up 8.7 cents at $2.276 per million British thermal units.

Most of the Southwest was forecast to see dry and warmer-than-normal spring temperatures through next week. The California coast was called to see seasonal readings in the high-60s to low-80s degrees Fahrenheit.
A warm, dry weather system was expected to stay over the Northwest into next week with well-above normal readings likely in the southern region.
